sentence: Targeted client communication reminders sent by mobile phone may slightly increase antenatal care use (mean difference 1.5, 95% CI –0.36 to 3.36), but this is low-certainty evidence and the interval includes no effect [3].

Targeted client communication via mobile devices may increase attendance for vaccinations compared with non-digital targeted client communication (RR 1.13, 95% CI 1.00 to 1.28; low-certainty evidence), and may make little or no difference to oral hygiene practices (low-certainty evidence) [3].
It found that we do not know whether these tools make healthcare workers better at following recommended practice, because the evidence was of very low quality [2].
For patient messages alone, some may improve service use, such as attendance at vaccination appointments, but the evidence is mostly of low or very low certainty [3].
For decision-support tools alone, it is not known whether they improve health workers' practice, and there is no clear pattern of effects on patients' health [2].
